dedupe_keys.name: ntia extended hata ehata urban propagation model

description: The Extended Hata (eHata) urban propagation model is a C++ reference implementation from the Institute for Telecommunication Sciences of the US National Telecommunications and Information Administration. It was developed for NTIA Technical Report TR-15-517, 3.5 GHz Exclusion Zone Analyses and Methodology, and extends the Hata-Okumura empirical model with terrain and environment corrections. Inputs are a terrain profile in the ITM format from mobile to base station, frequency, the heights of the mobile and the base station, an NLCD land-cover environment code and a reliability quantile; the output is path loss in dB, with an optional structure of intermediate values for debugging. Coverage: mobile paths in the United States, where NLCD codes apply, and elsewhere with equivalent land-cover classes. Format and access: source on GitHub, part of the ITS Propagation Library, releases up to v3.2; as a US Government work it is free of charge, with no US copyright and an NTIA disclaimer instead of a licence. Caveats: an empirical model with a stated frequency and distance range; urban clutter is statistical; documentation on the PropLib wiki is still being written. Simulation uses: coverage of mobile networks and exposure of base-station links to terrain and clutter, and spectrum sharing studies such as the 3.5 GHz CBRS exclusion zones. Related records: ITS ITM, P.528, P.2108 and LF/MF are the other PropLib models; SPLAT! and Signal-Server offer similar calculations.
